summary: Wooden front range light of 1880 at the Cheboygan River mouth, Michigan; a long keeper roster, then Coast Guard years, now volunteer keepers for the owning association.

lens.note: Sixth-order Fresnel; LighthouseFriends dates it to 1884, USLHS to 1880.

structures.type: lantern on tower atop keeper's dwelling

structures.note: LighthouseFriends says 1890; the Board's 1901 report says finished December 1900.

staffing.note: Volunteer keeper program run by the owner (GLLKA).

access.note: Open in season, weekends and some weekdays per GLLKA; hours may vary. USLHS record still says not open to the public.

stay.note: Volunteer keepers live in the lighthouse for a session; a small fee and GLLKA membership are required.

facts.ownership: Great Lakes Lighthouse Keepers Association (deed received June 2004)

events.note: Congress allocated $10,000 for range lights at the mouth of the river (31 July 1876).
Front light built as a lens lantern on a 9-ft square tower atop the keeper's dwelling; rear light a skeletal wooden tower.
Both range lights first exhibited on the night of 30 September 1880.
Sixth-order Fresnel replaced the lens lantern at the front light (LighthouseFriends). The USLHS record dates the original sixth-order lens to 1880.
Both range lights changed from fixed white to fixed red (LighthouseFriends).
Front light and keeper's dwelling moved to a new site; work begun in the year to June 1891.
$1,750 for additional land at the front range light listed in the Board's report.
Bulkhead at the Cheboygan River range had bulged out; repaired and straightened (Board's report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1899).
Steel tower replacing the rear range's timber beacon finished December 1900 (Board's report, fiscal 1901). LighthouseFriends gives 1890.
Deed to the adjacent land obtained (LighthouseFriends).
Range lights' intensity increased by changing the apparatus to reflectors, 27 June 1914.
Timber sheet-pile revetment for shore protection at the front light, $4,834, completed in the fiscal year ended June 30, 1921 (Commissioner's report).
Included in the first group of lighthouses excessed under the National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act of 2000.
Deed to the property received by the Great Lakes Lighthouse Keepers Association, June 2004.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends dates the steel tower replacing the rear range's timber beacon to 1890. The Light-House Board's report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1901 says the erection was finished in December, 1900. The story states both dates and gives the Board's date, from the report for the fiscal year that includes December 1900.

notes_for_editor: Lens date: LighthouseFriends gives a sixth-order Fresnel substituted in 1884; USLHS gives the original sixth-order Fresnel installed 1880. Unresolved; the story says so. The Light-House Board reports before 1891 are not in the local corpus, so 1880 first-light dates rest on LighthouseFriends and USLHS. Roster lines are the USLHS archive's own text and normalised roles from roster.py; 'at least' spans kept as documented; the 'USCG' lines carry no position name. Cheboygan River front range is not the rear range; the rear tower is mentioned only for the later-towers chronology. No storm, wreck or rescue tied to this light was found in the sources read, so the story has no storms chapter. The Northern Tribune notice of 30 October 1884 is read for the keeper's name only; its undated 'same date' change to fixed red is not relied on. Current Coast Guard status not checked. Newspaper search for the 1894 death returned nothing. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: facts only, with at most one short quotation in the story (none used). The Board's report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1894 lists $1,750 for additional land, earlier than the 1 July 1898 appropriation LighthouseFriends gives; the story states the gap and does not explain it. The 1921 revetment and the 1899 bulkhead are dated to their fiscal years, not to calendar years.
